guidance.procedure: Evaluate breadth, identification, and communication form as separate propositions after reading the complete operative definition. Technical-only coverage requires the protected class to remain exclusively technical; inclusion of business, financial, commercial, or other non-technical material opposes it. Explicit identification requires a universal marking or designation condition, while coverage regardless of labeling opposes it. For oral or visual information, preserve any contemporaneous designation and later written-confirmation requirements. Cite every fragment needed to complete the applicable definition or condition, but exclude headings, illustrative categories that add no rule, and unrelated neighboring clauses.

Run three independent lifecycle tests. First, identify the exact return-or-destruction trigger: a request-only duty does not establish a termination-triggered duty. Second, inspect the disposition scope and exceptions: a command covering all information and copies without an archival, backup, legal-retention, or dispute exception opposes permissible retention even if its trigger is only a request; an express exception supports retention. Third, require obligations expressly continuing beyond termination for survival, rather than treating a fixed agreement term as survival. Cite the operative trigger, disposition, exception, and continuation fragments only; exclude certificates, headings, severability terms, and adjacent lifecycle text that answers another test.

Match actor, action, recipient class, quantifier, and conditions independently. Employee access answers the employee proposition but does not itself authorize disclosure to advisers, agents, contractors, affiliates, or unrestricted third parties. An employee-only rule combined with a third-party prohibition supports the restrictive boundary; discretionary prior written consent is not a standing permission. For copying, distinguish an absolute no-copy obligation from an operative necessity- or purpose-limited exception. Cite every annotated fragment carrying the authorization, prohibition, recipient class, or condition, but exclude generic confidentiality duties, recipient-responsibility clauses, safeguards, headings, and adjacent use restrictions.

Trace each exception as a grammatical chain from any operative exclusion lead-in to the responsive subparagraph. Independent development requires development without use of, reference to, or access to protected information. Third-party acquisition requires an external source entitled to disclose and, when stated, free of a confidentiality duty; public-domain and prior-possession exceptions are not substitutes. Compelled disclosure permission and a notice duty are separate: verify legal compulsion, whether notice is required or excused, protective-order opportunity, and any required-portion limit. Cite the lead-in when it supplies the exclusion or scope and every responsive continuation, but not a standalone heading or neighboring exception.

Resolve actor, modality, action, object, scope, and exceptions separately for every proposition. Reverse engineering requires direct reverse-engineer, decompile, disassemble, decipher, or equivalent language concerning protected material; definitions, confidentiality, ownership, copying, and limited-use clauses are not substitutes. No-license requires express no-grant, no-license, or no-right language, not ownership alone. Agreement confidentiality requires protection of its existence, terms, discussions, or negotiations. Solicitation requires recruiting, soliciting, inducing departure, hiring, or comparable conduct directed at the specified people. Limited use requires an operative restriction to the stated purpose and any purpose definition needed to delimit it. Cite only independently responsive operative fragments.
